scenes.title: Meet Adhya
scenes.heading: A signature is not the whole story
lines: Hi, I'm Adhya, your AI learning mentor. Today, we'll practise inviting someone to a community survey.
Our goal is not to collect a signature. It's to protect a person's choice.

scenes.title: Notice the pressure
scenes.heading: Would you feel free to say no?
points: A college badge can create pressure
lines: Imagine a student tells a busy shopkeeper, our college needs everyone to answer.
The shopkeeper signs while serving customers. Does that signature prove the choice was voluntary?

scenes.title: Make a prediction
scenes.heading: Predict before I explain
lines: Pause here. Choose the strongest reason to question this consent.
Think about what the person understood, and whether saying no really felt possible.

scenes.title: Explain without pressure
scenes.heading: Explain. Check. Accept.
points: Ask them to explain it back
lines: Start again. Explain the purpose, time required, questions, data use and foreseeable risks in everyday language.
Make clear that declining, skipping a question, or stopping will not bring a penalty.

scenes.title: Check understanding
scenes.heading: A conversation, not a checkbox
lines: Then ask the person to describe what participation involves, in their preferred language.
If they seem uncomfortable, pause. If they decline, thank them and stop. Consent is ongoing, not a one-time checkbox.

scenes.title: Protect the answers
scenes.heading: Collect less. Protect more.
points: Never send identifiers to an AI tool
lines: For our fictional library survey, names and phone numbers are usually unnecessary. Use non-identifying response codes.
Store any required consent records separately. Never upload participant identifiers or sensitive raw responses to an AI tool.

scenes.title: Try a new situation
scenes.heading: What changes when a leader is present?
points: A leader says everyone must answer
Decide what to change before collecting data
lines: Now a community leader says everyone must answer, and a resident agrees. What should you change before collecting any data?
Choose your response. Use what you learned about power and voluntary choice, not just the word yes.

scenes.title: Take it into practice
scenes.heading: Practise the conversation
lines: Draft a ninety-second invitation, role-play a refusal with a peer, and get your supervisor's approval before fieldwork.
This is a fictional learning exercise, not ethics approval. Explain in your own words why a signature alone is not enough.
